svg.title: thriller: module and carrier block diagram

g.text: thriller: module and carrier block diagram
Chipset on a potted DF40 mezzanine module (the FIPS 140-3 module); connectors, transducers and interfaces on the carrier. See hw/module.md, doc/hw.md, doc/fips.md.
thriller module: potted; FIPS 140-3 module boundary = loader domain + TPM + flash (hw/module.md)
Carrier: outside the module, inside the application device's seal
bitstreams, loader, supervisor, app; TPM blobs
Potting: whole card, both sides, except the two DF40
connectors; heatsink bonded to the FPGA before potting;
underfill on the BGA and the TPM.
lockdown, PHY reset, WAKE, tamper inputs
Mailboxes: A loader–supervisor, B loader–application, C supervisor–application (the module's service API, doc/api.md)
RMII MAC, ARP, IPv4, ICMP, UDP demux
frames to the module, MAC checked
through clock monitors; never the loader
Master SPI from the QSPI flash at power-up; multi-boot fallback to the second bitstream slot
Bitstream authenticated (RSA-2048) before decryption (AES-256-GCM); keys in eFuse; JTAG locked at enrollment
The bitstream carries the boot ROM, the three cores and the pairing keys;
the loader, supervisor and application run from flash under per-line Ascon-AEAD128
Core clock: 25 MHz oscillator -> PLL; clock and PLL-lock monitors in the security block
25 MHz from XO; reset = network policy
J1 DF40C-80DP-0.4V(51): power, control, ciphertext, MAC'd frames
J2 DF40C-80DP: audio, display, clocks, GPIO
fixture carrier only; unrouted in production
the only power into the module
TVS on data lines; ciphertext, log, packages
Everything on the carrier changes without touching the validated module.
Treat these parts as inside, or passing through, the application device's tamper-evident enclosure.
The module cannot authenticate its carrier: removal is detected (RTC backup loss, seal loop),
and an installed bit with a carrier identifier is checked at boot (R51, H13).
PB_N, enclosure switch, seal loop, carrier ID -> security block and supervisor
UART: session frames (ciphertext); status in recovery
ciphertext or MAC'd: safe to expose (flash, card, network, UART, sensor, TPM bus)
plaintext: accepted inside the application device's seal (R38)
control and tamper inputs; dashed = JTAG, fixture carrier only
clocks: the module's own 25 MHz inside; carrier clocks reach only the supervisor and application domains
power: 5 V in; the module's rails never leave the card
private connection inside the FPGA, never on a bus
Fills: yellow = loader core domain (the FIPS module logic); blue = supervisor core domain; green = application core domain; grey = mailboxes.
The dashed outline is the potted module and the FIPS 140-3 physical boundary; the TPM is an embedded validated module inside it; the flash holds only ciphertext and public data.
